title: Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2027
official_title: Making appropriations for Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Passed the House and was received in the Senate. This is one of the twelve annual appropriations bills; standalone House-passed appropriations bills typically are not taken up as-is by the Senate but instead get renegotiated and folded into a year-end package, and it would need 60 votes there.
summary: Sets fiscal year 2027 funding for the Department of Agriculture, rural development programs, the Food and Drug Administration, and related agencies. The largest pieces are the domestic nutrition programs — SNAP, WIC, and child nutrition — which together account for most of the bill, alongside farm, research, conservation, and FDA accounts.
brief: FY2027 funding for Agriculture, rural development, and the FDA, dominated by the SNAP, WIC, and child-nutrition programs.

top_lines.headline: Domestic Nutrition Programs
subs: $101.24B for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), including a $3B reserve
$8B for WIC and $37.9B for child nutrition programs
Sets the WIC fruit-and-vegetable cash voucher at 267% (children) and 428% (women) of the fiscal year 2020 amount

top_lines.headline: Food and Drug Administration
subs: $7.11B total for the FDA, including industry user fees
$1.28B for the Human Foods Program and $2.54B for the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research
Sets aside funds for unannounced foreign drug inspections and foreign seafood inspections

top_lines.headline: Farm, Research, and Rural Programs
subs: Funds USDA departmental offices, the Agricultural Research Service ($1.8B), and farm and conservation programs
Funds rural development, foreign food assistance, and related agencies
Caps USDA's vehicle fleet at its 2018 size absent advance congressional approval

sections.label: Title I — Agricultural Programs and Research

items.main: Funds USDA departmental offices and research agencies.
items.detail: Provides salaries and expenses for the Office of the Secretary and USDA management offices and funds the research mission area, including $1.8B for the Agricultural Research Service (with per-building construction and alteration limits) and $99.97M for the Office of Inspector General.

sections.label: Title IV — Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program

items.main: Funds SNAP, the largest single program in the bill.
items.detail: Appropriates $101.24B to carry out the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, of which $3B is placed in reserve (available through September 30, 2029) for use only as needed for program operations, and continues work-registration and program-integrity conditions.

items.main: Funds the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children.
items.detail: Appropriates $8B for WIC through September 30, 2028, requires at least $90M for breastfeeding peer counselors, and directs that the fruit-and-vegetable cash-value voucher be set at 267 percent of the fiscal year 2020 amount for children and 428 percent for women.

items.main: Funds school meals and other child nutrition programs.
items.detail: Appropriates $37.9B (available through September 30, 2028) to carry out the National School Lunch Act and Child Nutrition Act, including $18M to carry out section 19 of the Child Nutrition Act, $22.38M for studies and evaluations, and farm-to-school grants capped at $500,000 per recipient for fiscal year 2027.

items.main: Funds commodity and disaster food assistance.
items.detail: Appropriates $546.07M, of which $460M is for the Commodity Supplemental Food Program, $75M for the Emergency Food Assistance Act, and $10M for the Farmers' Market Nutrition Program.

sections.label: Title VI — Food and Drug Administration

items.main: Funds the FDA, including amounts derived from industry user fees.
items.detail: Appropriates $7.11B for FDA salaries and expenses, including $1.64B from prescription-drug user fees, $712M from tobacco product user fees, and other fee streams. Of the total, $1.28B is for the Human Foods Program, $2.54B for the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (with at least $10M for pilots to increase unannounced foreign inspections), $985.57M for the Center for Devices and Radiological Health, and $687.12M for the Center for Tobacco Products.

items.main: Caps the USDA vehicle fleet at its 2018 level.
items.detail: Allows the Secretary to purchase passenger vehicles only so long as the total purchased in fiscal year 2027 does not exceed the number owned or leased in fiscal year 2018, and bars increasing the fleet above the 2018 level without advance written approval from the Appropriations Committees.

criticisms.why: I can't say that I am surprised that my Republican colleagues want to cut yet another resource to help women and children get food. This bill reduces the fruit and vegetable benefit for mothers and young children under WIC, and this goes against actual science-based evidence that tells us what families need to stay healthy. Cutting these benefits leaves 5.3 million moms and kids without reliable access to fresh fruits and vegetables.
Pursuant to the provisions of clause 3(a)(1) of House rule XIII and sec.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. Bynum
featured_quotes.text: I can't say that I am surprised that my Republican colleagues want to cut yet another resource to help women and children get food. This bill reduces the fruit and vegetable benefit for mothers and young children under WIC, and this goes against actual science-based evidence that tells us what families need to stay healthy. Cutting these benefits leaves 5.3 million moms and kids without reliable access to fresh fruits and vegetables.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Taylor
featured_quotes.text: Through this bill, Republicans are making critical investments in American agriculture, considering to fund broadband expansion programs in rural regions like mine in Appalachian Ohio, and providing funding for critical community projects. Counties like those in my district have been left behind for too long when it comes to internet connectivity and repairing water infrastructure that our communities rely on every day. This bill delivers long-overdue support for rural Ohio families so they can have the tools they need to thrive.
